 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

 Misc. Appeal No. 622 of 2009
 Pramod Kumar And Others
 Versus
Ajay Rajawat And Others

Appearance:
 Shri R.P. Gupta - Advocate for appellant No.1.

Shri Vinod Pathak - Advocate for appellants No.2 & 3.
 None for respondents No.1 & 2.
 Shri N.S. Tomar - Advocate for respondent No.3/Insurance
 Order
1. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellants that service upon respondent No. 2 may be dispensed with.
2. Upon hearing learned counsel and considering the submissions, service on respondent No. 2 is hereby dispensed with at the risk and cost of the appellants.
3. With the consent of learned counsel appearing for the parties, the matter is heard finally.

4. This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants seeking enhancement of Rs.1,50,000/- in the compensation amount awarded by the First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior vide award dated 06.03.2009 in Claim Case No. 42/2008.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By the said award, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 1,87,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the claimants on account of death of Smt. Usha.
5.

The necessary facts for disposal of this appeal, in brief, are that on NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:14184 2 MA-622-2009 24.03.2008 at around 6:15 pm, the appellants' father,
Sobaran, was going on his bicycle with the appellants' mother and younger brother seated on it.
They were going along the roadside from Narayan Vihar Colony, Gole Ka Mandir, Gwalior, towards Vivek Nagar.

When they reached near the police outpost of the Mela on Race Course Road, the driver of mini bus bearing registration number MP-30-P- 0118, coming from the direction of Gole Ka Mandir, by driving the vehicle rashly and negligently hit the bicycle from behind.
As a result, the appellants' father, mother, and brother Rahul sustained grievous injuries.

Rahul suffered a fracture Pramod Kumar vs Ajay Rajawat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48006505/
1 in the collar bone of his left shoulder.

Sobran Singh (father) died on the spot due to the accident,
and the mother Smt. Usha died during treatment at J.A.H. Hospital.

A report of the accident was lodged at Police Station Gole Ka Mandir, Gwalior at Crime No.153/2008.
6.

entities.text: Police Station Gole Ka Mandir, Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellants/claimants that the learned Tribunal has assumed the income of the deceased Smt. Usha to be Rs.1,500/- per month, whereas, as on the date of the accident in March 2008, the minimum wage for an unskilled labourer was Rs. 2,651/-, which ought to be taken as the income of the deceased.
The multiplier has to be applied as 14, instead of 15.
The learned Tribunal has neither awarded any amount under the head of future prospects nor appropriately granted compensation under the conventional heads.
It is prayed that the amount of compensation be enhanced accordingly.

7. Per contra , learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Insurance Company has supported the award and submitted that the learned Tribunal has appropriately awarded the amount against Respondents No.1 and 2, and has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from the liability of paying compensation.
He further contends that, at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was not operating under a valid and effective permit.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14184 3 MA-622-2009 8.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the record.

9. After perusal of the record, it is found that the learned Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle had not possessed a driving license with an endorsement authorizing him to drive a transport vehicle.

However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd, (2017) 14 SCC 663, has held as under :
"60.4. The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also not in dispute that there was no valid and effective permit for the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
In the absence of such a permit, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation; however, it is liable to pay the compensation on the principle of 'pay and recover'.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Amrit Paul Singh and Another v. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. and Others, (2018) 7 SCC 558, has held as under :
"24.

sentences.text: In the case at hand, it is clearly demonstrable from the materials brought on record that the vehicle at the time of the accident did not have a permit.

sentences.text: That apart, they had not stated whether the vehicle had temporary permit or any other kind of permit.

The exceptions that have been carved out under Section 66 of the Act,
needless to emphasise, are to be pleaded and proved.
The exceptions cannot be taken aid of in the course of an argument to seek absolution from liability.
Use of a vehicle in a public place without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction.
We are disposed to think so in view of the series of exceptions carved out in Section 66.

The said situations cannot be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14184 4 MA-622-2009 equated with absence of licence or a fake licence or a licence for different kind of vehicle, or, for that matter, violation of a condition of carrying more number of passengers.

Therefore, the principles laid down in Swaran Singh [National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh, (2004) 3 SCC 297 and Lakhmi Chand [Lakhmi Chand v. Reliance General Insurance, (2016) 3 SCC 100] in that regard would not be applicable to the case at hand.

entities.text: Swaran Singh [National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh, (2004) 3 SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Lakhmi Chand [Lakhmi Chand v. Reliance General Insurance, (2016) 3 SCC 100]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That apart, the insurer had taken the plea that the vehicle in question had no permit.

It does not require the wisdom of the "Tripitaka",
that the existence of a permit of any nature is a matter of documentary evidence.
Nothing has been brought on record by the insured to prove that he had a permit of the vehicle.
In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer.

Therefore, the Tribunal as well as the High Court had directed that the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver.

The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swaran Singh [National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh, (2004) 3 SCC 297 and other cases pertaining to pay and recover principle."

entities.text: Swaran Singh [National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh, (2004) 3 SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In view of the law laid down in the aforesaid cases, the Insurance Company is liable to first pay the compensation to the claimants and is then entitled to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
12. As far as the enhancement of the amount of compensation is concerned, the learned Tribunal has assumed the income of the deceased to be Rs.1,500/- per month.
According to the evidence on record, she was engaged in stitching work and in preparing salwar suits, etc.
Considering the minimum wages for unskilled labour as declared by the Labour Department at the time of the accident, the monthly income of the deceased ought to have been assessed as Rs. 2,651/-.

Keeping in view the age of the deceased as 45 years, as recorded by the learned Tribunal in Paragraph 12 of the impugned award, the claimants are entitled to an addition of 25% towards future prospects.

The claimants are also entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium and Rs.30,000/- under the heads of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14184 5 MA-622-2009 loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Multiplier of 14 and dependency of the claimants as 2/3rd are appropriate,
looking to the age of the deceased and the number of dependents 13.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to the following compensation:

The other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.

15. Although the appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.1,50,000/- and have paid court fees on the said amount, however, in view of the decision of the Apex Court in Kavita Balthiya and Others vs.
Santosh Kumar and Another in Civil Appeal No. 8053/2024 (@ SLP (C) No. 16558/2024) , it is directed that the appellants shall pay the court fees on the remaining amount of Rs.1,84,140/- (i.e.,
Rs. 3,34,140/- - Rs. 1,50,000/-) within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
